text:
Gina (Sales): Halcyon asked if we can run a short Dedicated POC for a custom 34B model variant they forked from an OSS model. They need KMS-backed keys, private VPC, and catalog-like routing so their app can A/B with our hosted model. Can Eng confirm compatibility and rough POC pricing?

Liam (SE): Quick checks: what format are they providing the model in (HF .bin / ggml / onnx)? Tokenizer type? Any custom ops? Also what's their target qps/latency so we can size nodes.

Gina (Sales): They've uploaded a tar to S3: s3://halcyon-poc/halcyon-34b-quant.tar.gz. Tokenizer is SentencePiece, vocab ~51200. No custom ops claimed, but they say they compiled with a custom RMSNorm patch. Target: 200 qps steady, typical request ~150 tokens, P50 latency target <= 120ms. Need data residency in eu-west-1.

Priya (Solutions): Notes: 34B + RMSNorm patch could be ok but patch might change kernel choices. Recommend we run a quick compatibility sweep: tokenizer sanity, kv-cache shape, and inference kernel fallback. For POC we can do a Dedicated trial (dev pool) with 2x A100-ish nodes and enable int8 quant if model converts. Pricing estimate for a 2-week POC (dedicated dev pool + infra + SRE support): ~$8k one-time. If they want reserved monthly, base commit starts at ~$20k/month. This is very rough.

Noah (Eng-Infra): Runtime supports RMSNorm fine in most forks, but if the patch changes parameter ordering we'll need to add a conversion shim. We can attempt conversion to our canonical format. KV cache shape: confirm past_key_values dims match [layers, batch, seq, head_dim]. If tokenizer uses spm with custom normalization we need the tokenizer assets. Can we get a small model artifact + tokenizer files?

Gina (Sales): I uploaded tokenizer.json and sample payloads to the same bucket (path: s3://halcyon-poc/tokenizer/). Also requesting the security questionnaire answers from them — they said they'd fill ours but asked what we need for KMS.

sec-bot: Security checklist: for KMS-integrated POCs we require: (1) KMS key ARN and IAM envelope flow, (2) VPC peering or private link details, (3) data retention / logs retention policy, (4) completed SOC2 section of the questionnaire. If customer-managed KMS, we need a test key with limited scope.

Carmen (Legal): NDA inbound — if they want to ship custom model artifacts into our infra we need the inbound code/material clause signed. I'll ping legal ops for a one-way NDA and the standard model licensing checklist. Also we need confirmation that no PHI is in the sample data.

Liam (SE): I'll kick off a compatibility sweep. Plan: 1) Tokenizer load + roundtrip on the sample inputs, 2) Convert model to our canonical format, 3) Run a smoke gen for 64 tokens and check kv-cache continuity, 4) Perf run with 200 qps emulation to verify latency on dev pool. Command I will run:
```
python infra/tools/convert_model.py --input s3://halcyon-poc/halcyon-34b-quant.tar.gz --out /tmp/halcyon_converted --target-format redwood-canon
```
I'll post logs here.

Priya (Solutions): If conversion fails, fallback: spin a hosted-compatible variant (smaller context, batch tuning) and use routing policy to A/B with their variant so they still get functional behavior. Also prepare quantization matrices: q4_0, q4_k_maybe, and int8 to test tradeoffs.

Gina (Sales): Customer asked about model catalog visibility — can we add a private catalog entry for the POC so they can hit a stable model-id?

Noah (Eng-Infra): Yes, we can create a private catalog entry scoped to the customer in their VPC for the POC. It will require a small infra ticket and the converted model artifact. ETA: ~1 business day after conversion passes.

Priya (Solutions): Action items:
- Liam: run conversion + smoke (due EOD PST)
- Noah: prepare dev pool template and catalogue ACLs (due +1 day)
- Carmen: share NDA + licensing checklist with Gina (due today)
- Gina: collect completed security questionnaire from customer and KMS test key (due tomorrow)

Gina (Sales): Thanks — I'll update Halcyon and push for the questionnaire. If we hit tokenizer/patch issues I'll loop in Research to evaluate changes needed. :thumbsup:
